## ✨ Highlights

- 📈 **A trend per node on the fleet screen of `janusctl tui`** - each line ends with a sparkline of sessions, requests, connections, network traffic, CPU or memory over the last 1 to 30 minutes, every node against the same scale: a node that takes ten times the traffic of another draws ten times higher, an outage is a gap. `m`, `w` and `y` change the metric, the window and the scale.
- 🎨 **Themes and an options menu** - `M` opens bpytop-style options: Janus's own theme, bpytop's 16 and a 16-colour one, each seen as you move to it; graphs in braille, blocks or the Linux console's glyphs; the defaults of the dashboard, saved for the next run. See [janusctl](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/janusctl.md#the-dashboard-janusctl-tui).

Everything in this release is janusctl's: nodes, the Controller and the Terraform provider are as in v2026.10.10.

## 🖥️ The dashboard in the terminal

- **The fleet's trend**: sessions per second (the default), requests per second, connections, network traffic in + out (every interface but the loopback and the VLANs, whose parent carries their traffic), CPU or memory - `m` goes through them, then hides the column. `w` sets the window: 1, 5 (the default), 15 or 30 minutes. `y` sets the scale, always the same for every node: linear up to the fleet's largest value, which the column's header gives (`SESS/S 5m max 384`), logarithmic to see a quiet node beside a busy one, or 0 to 100 % for CPU and memory. `s` sorts the nodes by the metric now; `p` stops the trend's clock with the rest. The trend takes the width left: on a narrower terminal the address, then the version, the load and HAProxy's version make room for it. Nothing more is asked of the nodes - the dashboard already kept their last 900 rounds.
- **Themes**: `janus`, the default, looks exactly as before; bpytop's built-in theme and its 15 theme files - adapta, default_black, dracula, dusklight, flat-remix, flat-remix-light, greyscale, gruvbox_dark, gruvbox_dark_v2, kyli0x, matcha-dark-sea, monokai, nord, solarized_dark, whiteout -; and `tty`, your terminal's own 16 colours. With bpytop's, each panel's border takes the theme's box colour, the CPU, memory, network and HAProxy graphs its gradients, the cursor its selection; states (up, down, drain...) keep readable colours, the Controller's light ones on a light theme. bpytop's themes are their authors' work (Apache License 2.0).
- **The options (`M`)**, each changed with `←` and `→` and seen at once, with what it means under the list: the theme; the theme's background, or your terminal's own (its transparency); the colours - auto from `COLORTERM` and `TERM`, or truecolor, 256 or 16 forced, a theme's colours brought to the nearest; the graph symbols - braille, blocks (eight heights a row), or tty for the Linux console, whose font has no braille (half blocks, shades, square corners); rounded corners; the refresh; the fleet trend's metric, window and scale; the processes' order. Saved when the menu closes, in `~/.config/janus/tui.json` beside the contexts - what `m`, `w`, `y`, `+`, `-`, `s` and `r` changed meanwhile included.
- **`-theme NAME`** picks a theme for one run (the shell completion knows them), `-theme list` names them all.

## 📖 Docs

- [janusctl](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/janusctl.md#the-dashboard-janusctl-tui): the fleet's trend, with a frame of it, the options and the themes; `-theme` in the [reference](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/janusctl-reference.md#janusctl-tui).

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **janusctl**: `apt update && apt install janusctl`, or the release's `.deb`. Nothing changes for an existing context; the dashboard starts in Janus's theme until you choose another.
- **Nodes, the Controller, the Terraform provider**: rebuilt from the same code as v2026.10.10 - nothing to update for this release.
